**Finding: deviation (RENEWAL) — Article IV Term, paragraph p0049.**

- **Issue:** The only renewal provision lets the Licensor unilaterally extend the 36-month Initial Period by **seven years** ("at the option of the Licensor"), with no non-renewal notice right for us and no cap on renewal pricing. Automatic/unilateral multi-year renewals are walk-away territory, and the clause fails the fallback (≤60-day notice window, uplift ≤5%) on both renewal length and our ability to exit.
- **Internal conflict noted:** Articles IV.II and IV.III of the same paragraph already require extension "by mutual written" agreement, so the seven-year option sentence is inconsistent with the rest of the term provision — which strengthens the ask.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** Replaces the seven-year Licensor option with successive 12-month renewals by mutual written agreement, a 30-day non-renewal right for either party, and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%; the comment offers the 60-day/5% fallback.
